column1: # Lemmas that share one lexeme-id stem — a ratchet, not a report.
# Columns: stem
# `slug` folds accents away, so two words that differ only by one get a single
# stem. `lexemeId` then hands the bare id to whichever lemma the build reaches
# first and suffixes the other with its part of speech, which is why every row
# here names a real, shipped mislabelling: `lexeme:te` is tea, not the pronoun.
# Those ids are permanent — mastery is keyed on them — so the eight below are
# recorded rather than fixed. Every one is a `tilde diacrítica` pair, where the
# accent is the entire difference between two words; Spanish has no other kind.
# Two rules, both enforced by `checkStemCollisions` in scripts/build-dataset.ts:
#   A collision that is not listed here fails the build. For a new language that
#   is the right answer and the fix is a transliteration in its language module,
#   never a row here — German's schon/schön and fordern/fördern are this same
#   accident with none of the history. See docs/tasks/language-matrix.md §1.
#   The claim order is checked, not just the pair. It is decided by which source
#   file is read first, so moving `té` out of nouns.tsv would silently swap two
#   lexeme ids and move a learner's mastery with them. Item ids have
#   id-ledger.tsv to stop exactly that; this is the same guard for lexemes.
te
